summary: The sides people fight for (NpcFactions, scripts/npc/npc_factions.gd): which sides each faction is hostile to, how its fighters look (a peoples preset, garments by slot: the first one this build can dress in is worn, else the basic shirt and breeches in the faction's colours), what they carry, how steady they are, what they say and what is found on them. Built for the 1757 German Flatts raid (French marines in campaign dress and Canadian militia against the valley's militia), toughs, later city guards, and the sky crews (sky_crew: the Long Patience's men in the Drift set's deckhand dress, side 'sky', hostile to no one until a story's turn sets it: NpcFactions.set_hostile). No Native fighters here: those are consultation slots (docs/main_story.md, 'What the consultation rule means'); NpcFactions also refuses Eastern Woodlands and Native-descended presets for any faction.
_doc: side: the side a faction fights on; 'player' is the player's own. hostile: the sides it attacks on sight (NpcFactions.set_hostile changes it at run time: a story's turn).

looks: peoples presets (assets/character/body/peoples.json), one picked per fighter. outfit: slot -> garment ids wanted, best first (the first PlayerOutfit.usable one is worn: cloth2 garments of the catalog); outfit_mix: slot -> {id: weight} ("-": nothing there), each fighter's garment of that slot picked by weight among the usable ones; drop_under: outer id -> slots that coat hides entirely (taken off: a veste under the closed capot); garment_colors: garment id -> its zone colours when worn (zone index -> palette token, or {"preset": a name of the catalog entry's extra.presets}, PlayerOutfit.resolve_colors), a list being one choice per fighter (of whole colour dictionaries, or of one zone's tokens); colors: the basic dress's zone colours (shirt_tucked zone 0/1, breeches zone 0/1/2) for slots none of those fill, lists the same (NpcFactions.outfit_of).

weapon: 'musket' or '' (melee only). sidearm: 'axe' (a hatchet or felling axe in the hand: for a man with no musket; one with a musket has his hands full and clubs with its butt), 'club' (the musket's butt) or ''. aim_s, reload_s: seconds. skill 0..1: how close the ball goes to where he aims. courage 0..1: how hurt he must be, or how many of his side fall, before he runs.
loot: pack kinds and counts left on the body (InventoryState kinds); the weapon carried is added to it.

talk: Je n'ai rien à vous dire.

militia.label: Militiaman
militia._dress_note: 2026-10-03: the Palatine farmer militia of German Flatts in 1757 was not uniformed: each man in his own working dress (a frock coat in a homespun colour, a few in blue; a long waistcoat in red, brown or drab; half in round hats; a black or check neckerchief, a few in a stock; some roused from bed with no coat). The blue-and-buff of every man before was the Continental Army's of 1775-83.

talk: Stay inside the walls after dark.
Good to see a friendly face.

city_guard.label: Watchman
city_guard._source: A colonial town's watch (2026-10-03; it was an invented black-coated soldier's uniform with no source): the watch of New York and Albany in the 1750s was kept by householders and hired watchmen in their own clothes, a drab or brown coat and a round hat, walking the streets at night with a staff, a lantern and a rattle (New York's Common Council watch ordinances; the Albany Minutes of the Common Council), doubled in wartime. No cartridge belt. The staff, lantern and rattle need models: until they exist the watch keeps a musket, as the armed watch of the war years. A garrison guard would be the regulars' (coat_regimental_1751, preset 22nd_foot), not this faction.

sky_crew.label: Sky crewman
sky_crew._dress_note: 2026-10-03: the 18th-century sailor's dress leads (70/30): a waistcoat or a sea jacket on a share of the men, tar hats on some, the harness on the riggers only, the mote belt on the casters; one glow per man (a jacket's night-watch cord drops the belt and the harness: drop_under).

talk: Don't look down, and don't look up too long.

ring_team_a.label: Competitor
ring_team_a._doc: Tidebreak, the ring sport (the owner, 2026-10-04): the player's side of the ring (side 'player': his teammates, the 3 v 3 to come). Element bots (NpcSquad opts element, tactics bend): no weapon, no barks (nothing said, no words over a head in the ring), the element side's ring dress (element_dress[element]: slot -> {id, colors}, NpcSquad.element_look; the catalog's set ring, tools/asset_author/build_ring_garments.py, 2026-10-05: earth the ochre wrap tunic, wrapped trousers, moss sash, arm wraps, shoes; water the blue fur-trimmed parka, fitted trousers, belt, fur-topped boots; fire the red sleeveless top with its gold collar, fitted trousers, sash, wrist guards, shoes; air the marigold long tunic, wide saffron trousers, sash, shoes; the player's arena dress is the same, PlayerAppearance.ring_dress); outfit, garment_colors and colors are the plain undyed dress of a fighter of the side with no element.

ring_team_b.label: Competitor
ring_team_b._doc: Tidebreak, the ring sport (the owner, 2026-10-04): the other side of the ring, hostile to the player and to ring_team_a. Element bots (NpcSquad opts element, tactics bend): no weapon, no barks (nothing said, no words over a head in the ring), the element side's ring dress (element_dress[element]: slot -> {id, colors}, NpcSquad.element_look; the catalog's set ring, tools/asset_author/build_ring_garments.py, 2026-10-05: earth the ochre wrap tunic, wrapped trousers, moss sash, arm wraps, shoes; water the blue fur-trimmed parka, fitted trousers, belt, fur-topped boots; fire the red sleeveless top with its gold collar, fitted trousers, sash, wrist guards, shoes; air the marigold long tunic, wide saffron trousers, sash, shoes; the player's arena dress is the same, PlayerAppearance.ring_dress); outfit, garment_colors and colors are the plain undyed dress of a fighter of the side with no element.
